Main.sentence: David D. McKiernan (born 11 December 1950) is a retired ___E:United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ ___E:four-star general U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_(United_States))___ who served in ___E:Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan)___ as Commander, ___E:International Security Assistance Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Security_Assistance_Force)___ (ISAF).
He served concurrently as Commander, United States Forces – Afghanistan (USFOR-A) from 6 October 2008 to 15 June 2009.

Prior to Afghanistan, McKiernan was Commanding General, ___E:United States Army, Europe and Seventh United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_United_States_Army)___ from 14 December 2005 to 2 May 2008.  Before promotion to four-star rank, he served as Commanding General, ___E:Third United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_United_States_Army)___ and ___E:Coalition Forces Land Component Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalition_Forces_Land_Component_Command)___ from 2002 to 2004, where he commanded all allied ground forces during the ___E:2003 invasion of Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq)___ , and as Deputy Commanding General, ___E:United States Army Forces Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Forces_Command)___ , the army's largest major command, [citation needed] from 2004 to 2005.

___E:Secretary of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense)___ ___E:Robert Gates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Gates)___ said new leadership was needed as the administration of President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ launched a new strategy in the seven-year-old War in Afghanistan.

McKiernan was replaced by two generals, General ___E:Stanley A. McChrystal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_A._McChrystal)___ (Commander) and Lieutenant General ___E:David M. Rodriguez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_M._Rodriguez)___ (Deputy Commander), ISAF and USFOR-A.

McKiernan graduated from the ___E:College of William & Mary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_William_%26_Mary)___ with a ___E:Bachelor of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ degree in history in 1972. He was commissioned from the ___E:Reserve Officers' Training Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Officers%27_Training_Corps)___ and entered active duty as an ___E:Armor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armor_Branch)___ officer.

He holds a ___E:Master of Public Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Public_Administration)___ degree from ___E:Shippensburg University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shippensburg_University)___ and an ___E:honorary doctorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_doctorate)___ in public service from William & Mary.

McKiernan gained experience in the ___E:Balkans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balkans)___ as a ___E:staff officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staff_officer)___ in the 1990s.

In July 1996, McKiernan joined the ___E:Allied Rapid Reaction Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_Rapid_Reaction_Corps)___ , serving as the Deputy Chief of Staff G2/ ___E:G3 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operations_(military_staff))___ , forward deployed in both ___E:Sarajevo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo)___ , ___E:Bosnia-Herzegovina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia-Herzegovina)___ and ___E:Rheindahlen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheindahlen_Military_Complex)___ (Mönchengladbach), Germany.

From August 1998 until September 1999, he served as Deputy Chief of Staff, Operations, Headquarters, United States Army, Europe and Seventh Army during a period of simultaneous operations in Bosnia, ___E:Albania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albania)___ , and ___E:Kosovo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo)___ .

Prior to these appointments McKiernan served in the ___E:VII Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VII_Corps_(United_States))___ Headquarters during the ___E:Gulf War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War)___ and then as the G3 in the 1st Cavalry Division (approx 1992–3) in the rank of ___E:lieutenant colonel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_colonel_(United_States))___ .

The first appointment was probably his first experience of working with other officers or formed units of other nationalities, in the second he had British Exchange Officers on his staff. [citation needed]
In 2001, McKiernan was assigned as G3 (Operations), ___E:Headquarters, Department of the Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters,_Department_of_the_Army)___ .

Following that posting, in September 2002, General McKiernan assumed command of the ___E:Third United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_United_States_Army)___ and ___E:United States Army Forces Central Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Central)___ , and became the ___E:Coalition Forces Land Component Commander U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalition_Forces_Land_Component_Command)___ for ___E:United States Central Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Central_Command)___ in preparation for ___E:Operation Iraqi Freedom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Iraqi_Freedom)___ .

In March 2003, McKiernan led all coalition and United States conventional ground forces that attacked Iraq to remove ___E:Saddam Hussein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein)___ from power.

Following his assignment as ground forces commander, McKiernan was assigned as Deputy Commanding General/Chief of Staff for ___E:United States Army Forces Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Forces_Command)___ , the largest major command in the Army which is responsible for the readiness and deployment of army forces based in the United States.
Then he assumed command of Seventh Army/United States Army Europe.
He was then assigned to Afghanistan as Commander, International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) and United States Forces-Afghanistan from 3 June 2008 to 15 June 2009.

In their book, Cobra II , military historians ___E:Michael Gordon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Gordon_(journalist))___ and ___E:Bernard E. Trainor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_E._Trainor)___ suggest that McKiernan was unhappy to hear of the cancellation of the deployment of the 1st Cavalry Division, a 17,000-soldier force that was scheduled to arrive in Iraq as a follow-on reinforcement.
Its deployment was cancelled on 21 April 2003, after U.S.
Defense Secretary ___E:Donald Rumsfeld U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Rumsfeld)___ raised the issue of whether it was needed.
Previously, shortly before the war, McKiernan won Pentagon approval for a new war plan that increased the number of ground troops, calling the new war plan COBRA II.
During Operation Iraqi Freedom, McKiernan had a different view of the battlefield than his superior, General ___E:Tommy Franks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Franks)___ .

McKiernan saw the ___E:Fedayeen Saddam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedayeen_Saddam)___ fighters as a major threat and one of the "centers of gravity" in Iraq, while Franks dismissed the importance of the irregulars.

The military was also surprised when McKiernan and his staff were not given command for post-war operations in Iraq, which instead went to V Corps and the newly promoted Lieutenant General ___E:Ricardo Sanchez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Sanchez)___ .

In a 2008 interview by Der Spiegel , McKiernan was asked whether Germany was a particularly difficult ally considering that its government requested limitations on its soldiers' deployment in Afghanistan, feeling that it might violate Germany's ___E:constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_constitution)___ if they were to conduct a ___E:targeted killing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Targeted_killing)___ in the absence of a direct attack.
McKiernan responded:
If ... the decision has been a legal and political decision back in Germany ...
I accept that. But as a soldier, I don't understand it. I don't understand ever putting your men and women in harm's way without their having the full ability to protect themselves.
That also means operating on actionable intelligence to defeat insurgents, and protect your forces.
That's how you keep your soldiers alive.
